The test run on this card's pull request failed twice because one automated test is broken on `main` — not because of anything this card changed.

This card's pull request adds a single written record (`docs/hand-built-proof-2026-10.md`) and touches no code. The failing test belongs to the planning-escalation feature, which checks that a retried escalation does not post its note a second time. The test fails, and it fails the same way on the last three `main` runs (starting at c0e68f6, 2026-10-09 about 22:45 UTC), so the card's work did not cause it and a rerun will not clear it. The cause is bad code that reached `main` from another change. The code now asks the card tracker where a card has been, and the test's stand-in tracker cannot answer. The code treats that as "ask again," so the note is posted twice and the test fails.

The fix needs a small code change on `main`: update the test's stand-in tracker, or the code's handling of a missing answer. A card should be cut for it, and this card's pull request can merge once `main` is green again. Until then, `main` stays red on every pull request. One earlier `main` run (c0e68f6) also failed a second test, `test_split_ledger.py::test_the_door_is_asked_for_the_window_start`. It passed on the two later runs, so it looks like a one-off.

Technical detail: `tests/test_planning_escalation_prior_answer.py::TestTheBlockReadsTheWholeThread::test_a_retry_whose_note_is_on_the_card_never_reads_it` fails with `assert outcome.parked and not outcome.posted`, because `scripts/planning_escalation.py` (about line 1274) calls `linear_ops.lane_history(identifier)` and the test's `_Lops` stub has no `lane_history` attribute (log: "could not read where the card has been ... asking again"). Run 38002376674 was job "scripts unit tests (part 4)" at head 2ae86ef; the result was 1 failed, 5215 passed.
